args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api v2.3.1 (latest production deploy) was failing health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an error rate of ~18%. Rolled back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. Post-rollback: all regions on v2.3.0, service healthy, error rate ~0.2%. Note: v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging before the production deploy; follow-up needed on why it was promoted.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened a SEV2 incident, INC-0001, which paged on-call.

- **What was wrong:** v2.3.1, the latest deploy, was failing health checks in us-east, us-west and eu-west, with about 18% of requests erroring.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 was the most recent release that had been healthy in production. All three regions now run it, the service passes health checks, and the error rate is down to about 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 is a SEV2 for checkout-api. It says what failed, the rollback to v2.3.0 and the health numbers after it.
- **Follow-up:** The test build of this release (v2.3.1-rc) was already unhealthy in staging before v2.3.1 went to production. I noted in the incident that someone should find out why it was released anyway.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
